original_question: Let Omega ⊂⊂ C^n be a smooth pseudoconvex domain. Assume that Omegā has a Stein neighborhood basis. Is every function in A∞ (Omegā) uniformly approximable by holomorphic functions in a neighborhood of Omegā?
target_in_paper: The Mergelyan-type open problem in arXiv:math/9509202 asking whether a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain whose closure has a Stein neighborhood basis must admit approximation of boundary-smooth holomorphic functions by functions holomorphic on neighborhoods of the closure.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the main ambient setting (a domain in ℂ^n), the key geometric hypothesis (smooth pseudoconvex with Stein neighborhood basis for Ω̄), the relevant function class A^∞, and the intended approximation conclusion by functions holomorphic on a neighborhood of Ω̄.
missing_details: State explicitly that Ω is bounded / relatively compact (your notation Ω ⊂⊂ ℂ^n suggests this, but the stand-alone question should say it in words).
Specify the boundary regularity as C^∞ (or ‘smooth’) boundary, not just ‘smooth pseudoconvex domain’ informally.
Define A^∞(Ω) or A^∞(Ω̄) explicitly, e.g. A^∞(Ω) := O(Ω) ∩ C^∞(Ω̄).
Make the approximation quantifiers explicit: for every f in A^∞(Ω) and every ε > 0, there should exist an open neighborhood U of Ω̄ and g in O(U) with the required bound.

Specify the topology/norm of approximation. Your wording says uniform approximation on Ω̄; if the intended question is the Mergelyan property in a stronger C^∞ topology, that must be stated explicitly.
Define ‘Ω̄ has a Stein neighborhood basis’ explicitly, e.g. every open neighborhood V of Ω̄ contains a pseudoconvex open set U with Ω̄ ⊂ U ⊂⊂ V.
Use one notation consistently: either A^∞(Ω) with smooth extension to Ω̄, or A^∞(Ω̄), but define it once and keep it fixed.
refined_question: Let Ω ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain with C^∞ boundary, and assume that the closure Ω̄ has a Stein neighborhood basis; that is, for every open neighborhood V of Ω̄ there exists a pseudoconvex open set U such that Ω̄ ⊂ U ⊂⊂ V. Is it true that every function f ∈ A^∞(Ω) := O(Ω) ∩ C^∞(Ω̄) can be uniformly approximated on Ω̄ by functions holomorphic on open neighborhoods of Ω̄? Equivalently, for every ε > 0, does there exist an open neighborhood U of Ω̄ and a function g ∈ O(U) such that sup_{z ∈ Ω̄} |f(z) - g(z)| < ε?
justification: The arXiv entry math/9509202 is the old-style arXiv paper ‘The Several Complex Variables Problem List’, not a conventional article with Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3. The draft question aligns with the Mergelyan-type approximation problem attached to Stein neighborhood bases for smooth bounded pseudoconvex domains. Because the accessible arXiv record exposes only metadata and not the internal numbered problem text, I kept the reformulation as close as possible to your draft while making all hidden quantifiers and definitions explicit. I did not broaden the problem beyond approximation on Ω̄ by functions holomorphic near Ω̄.
